definitions.explanation: A vivid red-orange color traditionally derived from cinnabar (mercury sulfide), associated with shrines and traditional art.

examples.japanese: {朱|しゅ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まった→染まる：04254_somaru⟧⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧。
examples.english: A torii gate painted in vermillion.

examples.japanese: {朱|しゅ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鮮|あざ}やか→鮮やか：05702_azayaka⟧だ。
⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{朱|しゅ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{答案|とうあん}→答案：03451_touan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{添削|てんさく}→添削：06837_tensaku⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The teacher corrected the exam paper in red ink.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漆器|しっき}→漆器：13329_shikki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{朱|しゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{塗|ぬ}って→塗る：01174_nuru⟧⟦{仕上|しあ}げる→仕上げる：04664_shiageru⟧。

notes:
A vivid red-orange color that has deep cultural significance in Japan. Originally referred to cinnabar, the mineral pigment used to produce the color.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {朱|しゅ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧: be dyed vermillion
- ⟦{朱色|しゅいろ}→朱色：20098_shuiro⟧: vermillion (the color name)
- {朱|しゅ}{塗|ぬ}り: vermillion-lacquered
- {朱|しゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: add corrections in red; also, to make corrections or revisions
- ⟦{朱肉|しゅにく}→朱肉：06192_shuniku⟧: red ink pad (for stamps)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧: red — the general word for red; {朱|しゅ} is more orange-tinged and culturally specific
- ⟦{紅|べに}→紅：13862_beni⟧/⟦{紅|くれない}→紅：20669_kurenai⟧: crimson, deep red — a cooler, bluer red than {朱|しゅ}
- {丹|に}: red earth pigment — an older, more literary word for red pigment

CULTURAL NOTE:
Vermillion is the iconic color of Shinto ⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧ gates and many shrine buildings. It was believed to ward off evil spirits. The expression {朱|しゅ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{交|まじ}われば→交わる：18379_majiwaru⟧⟦{赤|あか}く→赤い：00585_akai⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ ("if you mix with vermillion, you turn red") is a proverb meaning you are influenced by the company you keep.
